name: Alpheus

profile.address: 1905, East 6th Street, Holly, Austin, Travis County, Texas, 78702
profile.reading:
This facility sits at 1905 East 6th Street in the Holly neighborhood of East Austin, Texas, a historically industrial and residential district along the Colorado River just east of downtown and a short distance from the bars and entertainment venues of Austin's better-known 6th Street strip. It was built out and long operated under the Alpheus name by Alpheus Communications, a Texas regional fiber-optic network and data center provider that served the Dallas–Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio, and Houston corridor with its own facilities, including this one and a separate data center in Fort Worth.

On January 3, 2018, LOGIX Communications, later rebranded LOGIX Fiber Networks, completed its acquisition of Alpheus, with financial terms undisclosed. The deal expanded LOGIX's fiber footprint to more than 5,800 route miles and 180,000 fiber miles across Texas, and the combined company connected to roughly 75 Texas data centers while continuing to operate facilities across the Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, and Houston markets. Alpheus's employees and customers were absorbed into LOGIX rather than continuing under a separate brand, and this building today operates and markets as "LOGIX Austin (1905 E. 6th Street)" rather than under the Alpheus name, though the Alpheus name persists in older industry references and in this record's operator field.

LOGIX's own site describes the current facility as a carrier-neutral colocation building offering dedicated cabinets, cages, and private-suite configurations on a 36-inch reinforced raised floor, with A/B diverse power feeds, a 100% uptime SLA on power, redundant electrical and cooling systems, and pre-action dry-pipe fire suppression. It is audited to SSAE-18 and SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II standards, with HIPAA and PCI compliance capability, and is staffed with 24/7 network-operations-center monitoring and remote-hands support. LOGIX does not publish the building's total square footage, IT power capacity in megawatts, or a formal uptime-tier certification (such as Uptime Institute Tier III), which is typical of regional carrier-owned colocation buildings that market on service and connectivity rather than headline capacity figures aimed at hyperscale tenants.

In sum: this is a long-operating, carrier-grade colocation and interconnection facility in central Austin, now owned and branded by LOGIX Fiber Networks following its 2018 acquisition of Alpheus, offering audited, redundant infrastructure to network and enterprise tenants, without a published capacity specification.

reading:
Alpheus Communications was a Texas regional fibre network and data centre operator serving the Dallas and Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio and Houston corridor. It ceased to exist as an independent company on 3 January 2018, when LOGIX Fiber Networks completed its acquisition and folded the network, the customers and the staff into the LOGIX brand. Everything carried under the Alpheus name since then is a stale attribution, and the value of this entry is in showing exactly how one such attribution survived for years and what the building underneath it actually is.

The registry holds one Alpheus facility, and it is in Austin rather than Fort Worth, which is what the operator record's headquarters field would lead a reader to expect. PeeringDB still lists three Alpheus facilities, at 1905 East 6th Street in Austin, at Two Shell Plaza on Walker Street in Houston, and at 307 West 7th Street in Fort Worth. Only the Austin building is in this registry. Two networks and one carrier, FiberLight LLC, record a presence at the Austin site.

The building at 1905 East 6th Street, Austin 78702, is a single storey structure of about 36,000 square feet in footprint and around 11 metres tall, on Travis appraisal parcel 0203090302. It entered OpenStreetMap through the City of Austin buildings import in November 2015 as an unnamed footprint. On 5 October 2017 a mapper added the name Alpheus DataCenter and, a minute later, a second name, CH3 Data LLC, so both the outgoing and incoming identities have sat on the same object since before the acquisition closed. The operator and data centre tags that put it into this registry were not added until 27 March 2025, more than seven years after Alpheus stopped existing.

City of Austin permit records for the address show a small but genuine carrier facility with a long history. A new electrical UPS was installed in September 2006 and an exterior fuel tank valued at 51,000 dollars was permitted that December. In May 2012 the owner remodelled the reception area of an existing telecommunication services office and installed an eight foot fence along the east side of the building. In October 2015 a permit was issued to add a back up diesel generator to what the description calls an existing administrative and business office and data centre, energised that December. Interior demolition followed in September 2018. In August 2019 the existing signage was removed and replaced with new channel letters, which places the visible change of identity between the LOGIX acquisition and the current CH3 Data name. In the autumn of 2019 the owner replaced a concrete pad, set a state approved 300 square foot prefabricated building on it, trenched power and telecom to it from the base building, and commissioned a fire alarm and clean agent suppression system for it.

So the facility is real and it is small. What is not established is any measure of its capacity. No IT load, no utility service size, no generator rating and no white space area has been published by Alpheus, by LOGIX or by the current occupant, and none appears in the permit descriptions. The ch3data.com domain served no readable content during this research, and the address it resolves to sits in a block registered to a separate Austin colocation company, which indicates where that website is hosted rather than who runs the building. The right disposition is to record Alpheus as a former operator, reconcile the Austin building against its current name, and treat the Fort Worth headquarters on this record as describing a different building that the registry does not hold.
